1 Introduction 
1.1 Purpose and intended use 
This document establishes DailyKhata's formal requirements baseline for the project 
team, supervisor and assessors. It translates the approved problem, user needs and scope 
into eight business requirements, 69 functional requirements and 26 non -functional 
requirements. The catalogue supports architecture, database and interface design, 
implementation and acceptance testing. It specifies intended behaviour; it does not assert 
that the application has been built or tested. [G1-G5, D1, D2, A3] 
All 38 canonical scope capabilities are represented, including all 27 Must Have 
capabilities. Optional requirements retain their approved Should Have or Could Have 
status. The baseline is feasible as a bounded four -student integration project using 
existing OCR and language -model capabilities, subject to the dependency and 
acceptance-target reviews recorded later in this document. 
1.2 Project overview and problem 
DailyKhata is a personal expense management application primarily designed for 
Pakistani users who frequently deal with paper receipts, cash transactions and informal 
expense tracking. It reduces the effort required to maintain personal or household expense 
records through receipt digitisation, OCR, quick cash expense capture, manual expense 
entry, automatic categorisation, user confirmation and correction, a structured Chart of 
Accounts, transaction history, spending summaries, item -level price history, semantic 
product classification and an AI Financial Assistant. 
Paper receipts and unrecorded cash purchases leave personal and household expense 
histories incomplete. Manual upkeep makes consistent recording difficult. Users need 
low-effort capture and reliable ways to review and understand spending. 
1.3 Product boundary 
The primary users are homemakers and household budget managers, university students 
and salaried professionals in Pakistan. A single account holder records personal or 
household expenses. Small shopkeepers are secondary direct users for petty cash and 
supplier expenses. Family members may review information with the account holder or 
receive a user -exported summary; they do not gain household roles, invitations or 
collaborative editing rights. The system is mobile -first and targets ordinary Android-class 
devices. [D1, D2, G1] 
The current product combines reviewed receipt digitisation, manual and text -based cash 
entry, an expense ledger, internal accounting mappings, semantic product classification, 
item-level price history, summaries and a read -only AI Financial Assistant. Voice, 
bilingual localisation, export, custom labels, extra views and image archive remain 
optional. Detailed exclusions and future scope appear later and are not current 
requirements.

4.2 Business requirement analysis 
The first six outcomes define the minimum product purpose. BR -007 and BR -008 add 
optional benefits without changing the intended market. No requirement promises 
measured financial savings, user retention or a market share. A saving suggestion is 
useful only when its arithmetic and assumptions are visible; the user remains responsible 
for deciding what to do. An expense record can be internally coherent even when the user 
has not recorded all real -world spending, so the assistant must distinguish recorded 
spending from total actual spending.

account holder reviews required fields, resolves inconsistent totals and confirms 
categories, then explicitly commits the expense. Only an active committed expense 
participates in summaries and price history. Every protected operation inherits the 
authentication boundary. The common actor, preconditions, trigger and rationale stated 
for each subsystem apply to its records; each requirement supplies its own behaviour, 
acceptance oracle and failure path.
